name: Chinastar Chinese character input
description: Chinese word-processing software using character-component codes and other methods for entry on a personal computer.

impact.note: One of several Chinese input and word-processing products; it eased entry for its own users, and little later work is known to rest on it specifically.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: A contemporary review described Chinastar’s Cangjie-based input, other methods, and a $199 traditional-character configuration.

evidence.supports: Review describes Cangjie, keyboard entry, training barriers and II-46 at $199.

events.caveats: Review reports a product and price, not purchaser numbers or first invention date. The model needed 640K memory, a 10 MB disk and compatible graphics.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in cited evidence for this scope, not a global priority claim.

research.note: Independent reader: Checked the 1988 review and comparison table, including II-46 configuration and nominal $199 price.

measures.subject: Chinastar II-46 traditional-character software
measures.conditions: 1988 nominal software price requiring compatible hardware, not a transaction or complete computer price.

evidence.supports: Review describes Cangjie, keyboard entry, training barriers and II-46 at $199.

caveats: One Cangjie implementation; source does not establish origins of all Chinese input methods or a dependency on Unicode.
